funder_origin_name: Lena P. Harvey Foundation (Leo M. Harvey family), via a 1971 gift to the American Technion Society
funder_current_name: Harvey Prize endowment fund established by Leo M. Harvey / Lena P. Harvey Foundation, with continuing Harvey family and American Technion Society support
funding_share_basis: The purse is two annual awards of USD 75,000 each, paid in full (>50%) from the dedicated Harvey fund created by the Lena P. Harvey Foundation's September 1971 donation to the American Technion Society; the Technion administers and confers the prize but the official prize site and Technion's own Hebrew announcements describe a named, ring-fenced prize fund ('קרן הפרס') established by Leo M. Harvey that makes the awards, continued 'in perpetuity' with support from the Harvey family. No evidence of Technion general-fund financing or of any second funder was found.
money_note: Two prizes of USD 75,000 each are awarded annually, paid from the Harvey endowment originating in the Lena P. Harvey Foundation's 1971 gift to the American Technion Society; the funding arrangement has not changed hands since 1971.
evidence_quote: The Harvey Prize is derived from a donation made by the Lena P. Harvey Foundation to the American Technion Society in September 1971. Two awards of $75,000 each are made annually.
judgment_reason: No published financial statement shows whether the Harvey fund is still segregated on Technion's books, so a coder could treat today's purse as Technion money (University, Israel). We keep Philanthropy/United States because the prize site and Technion's Hebrew releases refer to a named Harvey prize fund awarding the prizes 'in perpetuity' with continuing Harvey family support, and no source indicates the gift was pooled into general university funds.
